# Version history

- 2026-10-16: added cell seeds 2 and 3 (three cells per k), replacing the single seed-1 cell.
- 2026-10-16: moved here from `taxmarker-mislabel-tests.qmd`: the three setups on MislabelBench cells (family distance, 5%, seed 1).

# Summary

This report runs nf-core/taxmarker on cells of the MislabelBench grid [@mislabelbench], a benchmark that relabels 1% or 5% of 2,023 archaeal 16S sequences in groups of k sharing one wrong label.
It complements `taxmarker-mislabel-tests.qmd`, where one wrong-label group is injected into a bacterial reference.
A sequence the pipeline reports as mislabelled is said to be *flagged*.

- With sativa-epang alone, recall of injected sequences falls with k like the figures MislabelBench reports for sativa-epang, with a wide spread between cells at k = 5 (17-52 of 105 flagged in three cells).
- With clustering in front, the injected sequences that share a cluster with a flagged representative are 64-85% of all injected at k >= 3 in all three cells per k, against 16-50% for sativa-epang alone.
  That is the opposite of the single-group sets, where clustering lost all injected sequences.
- The price is on the other sequences: expansion adds 58-182 flags, and the share of flags that are injected is lower than for sativa-epang alone at k <= 3 (0.22-0.32 against 0.34-0.63), overlaps it at k = 5 (0.25-0.30 against 0.18-0.44) and is higher at k = 10 (0.30-0.38 against 0.23-0.27).
- Raxtax flags 91-95 of 101 injected sequences at k = 1, but only 6-12 of those are sativa-epang flags.

# The benchmark grid

MislabelBench relabels sequences of a database of N = 2,023 archaeal 16S sequences in groups, and varies three things [@mislabelbench].

- **Distance** says how far the wrong label is from the true one: the recipient lineage shares everything above the named rank with the donor lineage.
  With species distance a sequence gets the label of a sister species in the same genus; with class distance it gets a label from another class.
- **Rate** is the share of the database that is relabelled, 1% (about 20 sequences) or 5% (about 100).
- **k** is the number of sequences in one group: k sequences from one donor lineage all get the label of one recipient lineage.
  New donors and recipients are drawn until the rate is reached, so the number of groups is about rate × N ÷ k.
  A donor lineage has at least k + 1 members, so it always keeps at least one correctly labelled sequence.

| | k = 1 | k = 2 | k = 3 | k = 5 | k = 10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1% (about 20 sequences) | 20 groups | 10 | 7 | 4 | 2 |
| 5% (about 100 sequences) | 100 groups | 50 | 34 | 20 | 10 |

Rate and k are crossed: at a fixed rate a larger k gives fewer but larger groups, and a larger group outvotes the correctly labelled relatives of its donor.
A higher rate gives more groups and so more wrong labels in total.
Each combination of distance, rate and k exists as three cells that differ in which sequences are chosen (cell seeds 1-3).

The recall in this report is the fraction of the injected sequences that are flagged, and it should not be confused with the rate.
It generally rises with distance, because a sequence given a label from a distant lineage sits among relatives whose labels clearly disagree with it, whereas one given the label of a sister species lies next to its true relatives.
It falls with k and, more weakly, with rate.

The single-group sets of `taxmarker-mislabel-tests.qmd` differ in design: one group of k sequences, relabelled into one recipient taxon, in a bacterial reference.

# Results

## The three setups on three cells per k

To see whether the clustering result depends on the injection design, the three setups (sativa-epang alone, clustering with raxtax off, and the pipeline defaults) were run on cells of the MislabelBench grid [@mislabelbench]: family distance, 5% of the 2,023 archaeal sequences relabelled, k = 1, 2, 3, 5 and 10 sequences per wrong label, in the three cells (cell seeds 1-3) the benchmark provides for each k, plus the un-injected base set.
The input is its alignment and its taxonomy, with `--fast --seed 42` and `GTR+FO+I+R10` as elsewhere in this report (`scripts/run_mb.sh`, run on a 128-core server; results scored with `scripts/mb_cells.py`).
Here 101-110 sequences are injected in groups of k, each group with its own donor and recipient taxon, and no donors are deleted.
Flagged counts every method, so raxtax flags count as well; testable = injected sequences that reach sativa-epang after clustering and raxtax; expanded = injected sequences that are flagged or share a cluster with a flagged representative.
Added = flags on non-injected sequences that are not flagged at the same setup's base run.
The cell seed changes which sequences are injected; the pipeline seed is 42 throughout, so the spread between cell seeds is the spread between injections.
Table cells show the median over the three cells with the range in brackets.

```{r tbl-mb-cells}
#| label: tbl-mb-cells
#| tbl-cap: The three setups on MislabelBench cells (family distance, 5%; three cell seeds per k, pipeline seed 42, lwr > 0.9). Median over the cells with the range in brackets. Flagged and expanded are injected sequences; added counts flags on other sequences; injected share of flags is flagged injected sequences over all flags, which include the flags of the un-injected base set. Expansion adds every member of the cluster of a flagged representative.

med <- function(x, digits = 0) if (min(x) == max(x)) as.character(x[1]) else sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f (%.", digits, "f-%.", digits, "f)"), median(x), min(x), max(x))

read_tsv("data/mb_cells.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(cell_k > 0, distance == "family", rate == 0.05) %>%
  mutate(setup = factor(setup, c("alone", "cluster", "cluster_raxtax"), c("sativa-epang alone", "cluster", "cluster + raxtax"))) %>%
  mutate(share = flagged / (flagged + other_flags), share_expanded = flagged_expanded / (flagged_expanded + other_expanded)) %>%
  group_by(setup, k = cell_k) %>%
  summarise(injected = first(injected), testable = med(testable), flagged = med(flagged), `flagged by sativa-epang` = med(flagged_sativa),
            expanded = med(flagged_expanded), added = med(added), `added, expanded` = med(added_expanded),
            `injected share of flags` = med(share, 2),
            `injected share, expanded` = med(share_expanded, 2), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(setup, k) %>%
  kable()
```

sativa-epang alone flags 86-92, 65-73, 37-49, 17-52 and 20-21 of the injected sequences at k = 1, 2, 3, 5 and 10 (85-91%, 64-72%, 36-48%, 16-50% and 18-19%), a fall with k of the same shape as the one in the single-group sets.
These are close to the recalls MislabelBench reports for sativa-epang at this distance and rate (0.96, 0.67, 0.49, 0.23 and 0.20), except for the large spread at k = 5.
With clustering in front, only the 28 to 101 representatives are placed, and 79-81, 51-54, 32-42, 21-27 and 14-18 of the injected sequences are flagged, fewer than alone at k = 1, 2 and 10, and within the spread of alone at k = 3 and 5.
Counting the cluster-mates of a flagged representative as flagged gives 79-82, 67-76, 70-77, 67-73 and 79-80 injected sequences flagged, 64-75% at k >= 3 against 16-50% alone (64-85% with raxtax on).
The price is on the other sequences: expansion also flags all members of flagged clusters of untouched sequences, and the added flags go from 2-21 to 58-182.
Raxtax flags 91-95 of 101 at k = 1, but only 6-12 of those are sativa-epang flags; it removes flagged sequences from the tree before the placement, and the added flags are 8-47 without expansion, against 2-21 for clustering alone.
The injected share of all flags is 0.22-0.32 with expansion at k <= 3 against 0.34-0.63 alone, overlaps at k = 5 and is 0.30-0.38 against 0.23-0.27 at k = 10.

So the loss of injected sequences with clustering in the single-group sets does not reappear here, where each wrong label is carried by one group among many recipients.
Whether that is because the groups are spread over many recipients, or because the donors here are not the near-identical *S. aureus* sequences of the delete design, has not been tested.
It also means that the clustering result depends on how the injected sequences are spread, which the single-group design cannot show.
The three cells per k are three injections analysed with one pipeline seed (42), so the ranges do not include search variation.

## Other distances and rates

The same three setups were run on the first cell of every other combination of distance (species, genus, family, order, class, phylum) and rate (1% and 5%), k = 1, 2, 3, 5 and 10.
Family distance at 5% has three cells per k as above; the other combinations have one.
The distance is the taxonomic rank up to which donor and recipient lineage share their classification, so species distance moves a sequence to a sister species and phylum distance to a different phylum.

```{r mb-data}
#| label: mb-data
#| include: false

setup_lv <- c("alone", "cluster", "cluster_raxtax")
setup_lb <- c("sativa-epang alone", "cluster", "cluster + raxtax")
setup_col <- c("sativa-epang alone" = "#4d4d4d", "cluster" = "#1b7837", "cluster + raxtax" = "#c2541d")

cells <- read_tsv("data/mb_cells.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(cell_k > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    setup = factor(setup, setup_lv, setup_lb),
    distance = factor(distance, c("species", "genus", "family", "order", "class", "phylum")),
    rate = factor(rate, c(0.01, 0.05), c("1% relabelled", "5% relabelled")),
    flagged_share = flagged / injected,
    expanded_share = flagged_expanded / injected,
    share = flagged / (flagged + other_flags),
    share_expanded = flagged_expanded / (flagged_expanded + other_expanded)
  )

mb_theme <- list(
  facet_grid(rate ~ distance),
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 5, 10), trans = "log10"),
  scale_colour_manual(values = setup_col, name = NULL),
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
)

by_variant <- function(d, plain, expanded) {
  bind_rows(
    d %>% transmute(setup, distance, rate, k = cell_k, cell_seed, value = {{ plain }}, variant = "flagged itself"),
    d %>% transmute(setup, distance, rate, k = cell_k, cell_seed, value = {{ expanded }}, variant = "expanded to cluster")
  )
}
```

```{r fig-mb-recall}
#| label: fig-mb-recall
#| fig-cap: "Fraction of injected sequences flagged against k, by distance (columns) and rate (rows). Solid lines: a sequence counts only if it is flagged itself; dashed lines: it also counts if it shares a cluster with a flagged representative. Points are cells; family 5% has three per k, the rest one."
#| fig-height: 5.5

by_variant(cells, flagged_share, expanded_share) %>%
  ggplot(aes(k, value, colour = setup, linetype = variant)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("flagged itself" = "solid", "expanded to cluster" = "dashed"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "k (sequences per wrong label)", y = "injected sequences flagged") +
  mb_theme
```

```{r fig-mb-added}
#| label: fig-mb-added
#| fig-cap: "Flags on sequences that were not injected and not flagged in the same setup's un-injected run, against k. Line types as in the previous figure."
#| fig-height: 5.5

by_variant(cells, added, added_expanded) %>%
  ggplot(aes(k, value, colour = setup, linetype = variant)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = "sqrt", breaks = c(0, 10, 50, 100, 200)) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("flagged itself" = "solid", "expanded to cluster" = "dashed"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "k (sequences per wrong label)", y = "added flags on other sequences") +
  mb_theme
```

```{r fig-mb-share}
#| label: fig-mb-share
#| fig-cap: "Share of all flags that are injected sequences against k. The flags of the un-injected base set count as other flags. Line types as in the previous figures."
#| fig-height: 5.5

by_variant(cells, share, share_expanded) %>%
  ggplot(aes(k, value, colour = setup, linetype = variant)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("flagged itself" = "solid", "expanded to cluster" = "dashed"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "k (sequences per wrong label)", y = "share of flags that are injected") +
  mb_theme
```

## Runtime

Runtimes come from the Nextflow execution traces of the runs above (`scripts/mb_runtimes.py`).
Four runs shared the 128-core server at a time, each with 30 CPUs and 150 GB, so the times are indicative and not a speed benchmark.
The RAxML-NG search runs with `--fast --seed 42` on 12 threads, as set by the process label.
Wall is the time from the first task submitted to the last task finished.
The stage columns sum task durations: RAxML-NG search, sativa-epang placement (reference, tasks, placement, scoring and report), the clustering and raxtax pre-filters, and everything else (taxonomy, name check, gap filter, MultiQC).

```{r tbl-mb-runtimes}
#| label: tbl-mb-runtimes
#| tbl-cap: Median runtime in seconds per run on MislabelBench cells (family distance, 5%), over the n runs of each setup and k (k = 0 is the un-injected base set). Concurrent runs, `--fast --seed 42`, GTR+FO+I+R10.

read_tsv("data/mb_runtimes.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(parallel == 4) %>%
  mutate(setup = factor(setup, c("alone", "cluster", "cluster_raxtax"), c("sativa-epang alone", "cluster", "cluster + raxtax"))) %>%
  group_by(setup, k) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), across(c(wall, raxml, placement, prefilter, other), median), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(setup, k) %>%
  kable()
```


Over the 16 runs of each setup (the base set and the 15 injected cells) the median wall time is 155 s for sativa-epang alone (146-177 s), 198 s with clustering (170-231 s) and 179 s with clustering and raxtax (147-225 s).
The RAxML-NG search is half to two thirds of that.
It is longer with clustering (median 131 s against 84 s alone) although fewer sequences remain; the reason has not been examined.
The placement is shorter with clustering (28-30 s against 50 s), and the clustering and raxtax pre-filters cost 14 s and 25 s.
The same setup and k differ by tens of seconds between cells, so differences of that size are not meaningful.
